claim: For the mass-action family Xi<->2Xi plus transfers Xi->Xj on a strongly connected finite graph, let A(t) be its Metzler linear reaction matrix. If a supplied w>>0 satisfies 0<alpha<=(A(t)w)_i/w_i<=Gamma and 0<b_-<=b_i(t)<=b_+, then every nonnegative bounded mild Neumann solution is global; positive initial data are trapped between explicit scalar logistic multiples of w and eventually enter the diffusivity- and mesh-independent box [w_min alpha/(2 b_+ w_max), 2 w_max Gamma/(b_- w_min)].
quantifiers: Every m>=2, bounded domain with Neumann boundary condition, strongly connected transfer graph, measurable positive bounded rates satisfying (2) almost everywhere, every D_i>=0 (or conservative Markov diffusion generators satisfying the maximum principle and L_i 1=0), and every nonnegative continuous initial datum; positive weighted minimum is required for the lower permanence bound.
supplied_inputs: alpha, Gamma, b_-, b_+ essential bounds

costs.comparison_work: O(m+|E|) rate inequalities after w and margins are supplied
costs.rate_bound_verification: not supplied; arbitrary measurable rate paths require external certificates for essential bounds

baseline: Prior N54 common-scalar-diffusion all-endotactic theorem conditional on N33; finite-graph species-dependent transport update has no mesh-uniform bound. Primary indirect-diffusion theorems cover selected nonlinear/linear systems with additional assumptions. This result gives an explicit mesh-uniform box for a structured switched cooperative mass-action family.
falsifier: A classical solution of (1) with rates satisfying (2) leaving either logistic comparison bound; failure of the margin assumptions is outside the claim.
